leads.title: Bf-109 - Daimler-Benz Run-Up (Fight2FlyPhoto)
leads.licence: CC BY 3.0 (second-hand; not yet checked on the Freesound page)
leads.licence_evidence: I could not read the Freesound page. A third-party project, the GitHub repo griffio/www2-scramble (https://github.com/griffio/www2-scramble, page read), credits '"Bf-109 - Daimler-Benz Run-Up" by Fight2FlyPhoto, licensed under CC BY 3.0' and uses it pitched down as its Fw 190 engine sound. Confirm the licence on the Freesound page itself.
leads.what: From the search-result title: a ground run-up of a real Bf 109's Daimler-Benz inverted V12. The engine variant, location, date, mic placement and length are not shown in the snippet. The same uploader's Bf 109 startup clip (242179) is described elsewhere as a restored Bf 109E-3 with a DB 601. The uploader's other files are warbirds from the same events (P-47, Fw 190, B-25, Skyraider), which points to the Flying Heritage Collection at Paine Field, WA. Both points are inferences, not stated on a page I could read.
leads.fit: This is the best stand-in found: a real DB 601/605-family inverted V12 recorded outdoors. A run-up usually has a sustained high-power stretch that could be cut into a steady drone loop. Someone else has already used it as a WW2 engine loop source.
leads.concerns: It is a ground run-up, not in flight, so no Doppler or air movement, and rpm changes during a run-up. Length unknown, so it may not give 20 s of steady power. Possible wind, crowd or PA noise at an airshow. It is a DB engine, not a Jumo 211, so a stand-in only. The licence is second-hand until checked on Freesound.

leads.title: Messerschmitt Bf 109 Startup and Taxiing (Fight2FlyPhoto)
leads.licence_evidence: The Freesound page is blocked from here. Cities and Memory republished it in its 'Obsolete Sounds' project (https://www.mixcloud.com/citiesandmemory/messerschmidt-bf-109-startup/ and https://audioboom.com/posts/8146587-messerschmidt-bf-109-startup, both read), crediting 'Recording provided by Fight2FlyPhoto via Freesound', but neither page names a licence. The uploader's run-up clip (142898) is credited elsewhere as CC BY 3.0, so this one may be the same. Check on Freesound.
leads.what: Cities and Memory's description reads: 'A restored Messerschmitt Bf-109E-3 starts up its Daimler-Benz 601 engine.' Their copy runs 0:41. The Freesound title says startup and taxiing. Recordist: Fight2FlyPhoto. Location, date, mic placement and the original's length are not stated on the pages I read.
leads.fit: A real DB 601 in an original Bf 109E airframe (not a Merlin-engined Buchon), recorded outside. The idle and taxi parts could give a steady low-rpm drone layer.
leads.concerns: Mostly start-up and idle/taxi, not cruise power, so it is lower and lumpier than a formation drone. The startup transients would need cutting. Cities and Memory say their project remixes sounds, so use the Freesound original, not their copy. Length of the original unknown. Licence unknown until checked.

leads.title: Spitfires and Bf-109 Flyby (Fight2FlyPhoto)
leads.licence_evidence: Only the search-result title was visible. The licence may match the same uploader's run-up clip, which is credited elsewhere as CC BY 3.0, but nothing confirms that for this file.
leads.what: From the title: a flyby of Spitfires and a Bf 109, recorded by Fight2FlyPhoto, probably at the same Flying Heritage Collection events as the uploader's other warbird clips (an inference). Length, date, place and mic details unknown.
leads.fit: This is the only in-flight DB-engined Bf 109 recording found under a likely free licence. It could give the moving, airborne character that a ground run lacks.
leads.concerns: The Spitfires' Merlin engines are mixed in, and the Bf 109 may be audible alone only briefly or not at all. A flyby is a pass, not a steady drone, so a 20 s loop is unlikely. Possible crowd, wind or commentary. Licence unknown.

leads.title: Republic Aviation - P-47D Thunderbolt and Messerachmitt ME 109 start-up and make a fly-by at Paine Field USA 2009 with sound.ogv
leads.licence_evidence: Commons is blocked from here, so I could not see the licence. Commons videos are often CC BY-SA, which is NOT on the allowed list, so check whether it is CC BY, CC0 or PD.
leads.what: From the file title: a video, with sound, of a P-47D and a 'Me 109' starting up and flying by at Paine Field, USA, in 2009. Paine Field is home to the Flying Heritage Collection, whose Bf 109 E-3 has a DB 601, so this is probably that aircraft (an inference). Recordist, length and mic details unknown.
leads.fit: A real DB-engined Bf 109 starting and flying, recorded outdoors. If the Bf 109 is heard alone in a stretch, that could be cut as an in-flight stand-in.
leads.concerns: The P-47's R-2800 radial is in the same video and may cover the Bf 109. Video-camera audio is likely compressed and wind-affected. It is a pass, not a steady drone. Licence unknown and may be CC BY-SA.

leads.title: File:Bf109g10.ogv
leads.licence_evidence: Commons is blocked from here, so I could not see the licence. It may be CC BY-SA, which would not qualify.
leads.what: From the file name: a video of a Bf 109 G-10. Nothing else was visible: no aircraft identity, place, date, sound content or length.
leads.fit: Worth checking only if it is a real DB 605-engined G-10 filmed with live sound outdoors. That would give a DB 605 in-flight stand-in.
leads.concerns: Flying 'G-10' warbirds are mostly converted Hispano Buchons. Some have been re-engined with DB 605s, but others may still have Merlins. It may also be silent or archival wartime footage, which would be excluded. Low confidence.

leads.title: Ju88AJumo211_Genuine_extract.wav (forum attachment)
leads.licence_evidence: The forum thread (page read) gives no licence or source. The poster, BOBC, calls it an 'actual sound recording' and says it is a small part of a longer recording they hold.
leads.what: An audio extract said to be a Ju 88A's Jumo 211 starting up, idling, then taxiing. Who recorded it, where, when and with what equipment are not stated. Length unknown.
leads.fit: This is the only lead I found that claims to be a real Jumo 211, the correct engine for the Ju 87.
leads.concerns: Weak lead. Origin unknown, licence unknown, and it is only an extract. It may well come from the BBC's wartime sound-effects discs. The UAH archive lists a BBC Sound Effects He 111 recording from that era, and if this is BBC material the rules exclude it. Start-up, idle and taxi only, no cruise power. Probably old disc audio with surface noise. Use only if the poster can show a free licence and a non-library origin.

gaps:
I found no recording of a running Jumo 211 that is both clearly real and under a free licence.

No Jumo 211 appears to have been run in public recently:
- FHCAM's Ju 87 (the article calls it an R-2, wk.nr. 5709): its Jumo 211 was overhauled by Vintage V-12s in Tehachapi. The airframe moved to The Roost in Bentonville, Arkansas on 27 June 2025, and no engine run is reported.
- The American Heritage Museum's Ju 87D-5: its September 2026 update mentions no engine run.
- The Wings Museum (UK) Jumo 211 for Bodø: it only turns over by hand.
- 'White 1', mentioned in a June 2025 forum post, is FHCAM's Fw 190 D-13, which has a Jumo 213, not a 211.

So the Bf 109 stand-ins are the strongest leads. All of them still need their licence checked on the blocked pages (Freesound and Commons), and a Freesound 'Sampling+' or a Commons CC BY-SA licence would rule a file out.

I could not read any YouTube page; every fetch was rate-limited or failed. These titles are unverified for content and CC licence:
- 'Jumo 211 Motor - Engine' https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YhjdC4Yt6l0
- 'Junkers Jumo engine of a JU 88 bomber' https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=woX6OWRiXHI
- 'Ju-87 start engine' https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XWnr-5rZ5gM
- 'Junkers Jumo 211' https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RacYSErVi1s

None is confirmed to show an engine running, and several Jumo results were slideshows, simulator or RC-model videos.

I found no free-licence in-flight DB 605 recording. The best-known flying DB 605 Bf 109s are 'Red 7' G-4 D-FWME and Messerschmitt Stiftung G-6 D-FMBB, and they only turned up as photos or videos of unknown licence.

Deliberately excluded:
- UAH Archives 'World War II Aircraft: Heinkel HE-111 (German) (Interior)' (https://archives.uah.edu/repositories/2/archival_objects/93528). It is a genuine wartime He 111 recording, but the page lists its source as BBC Sound Effects (EC 500E), it has no licence, and it can only be heard in the reading room.
- craigsmith 'G04-07-WWII Stuka engine drone' (https://freesound.org/people/craigsmith/sounds/437771/): an excluded library series.
- Mastersoundboy2005 Stuka siren/scream clips, Sphyrna 'stuka01.mp3' (https://freesound.org/people/Sphyrna/sounds/69189/) and Farepello 'diveBomber.WAV' (https://freesound.org/people/Farepello/sounds/792800/): origin not shown, and they are likely designed or taken from films.
- YleArkisto 'Junkers, a 1936 model, taking off' (https://freesound.org/people/YleArkisto/sounds/256042/): almost certainly not a Jumo 211 (the aircraft type isn't named).
- DVIDS 'Junkers Ju 88D-1/Trop' video (https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1019037/junkers-ju-88d-1-trop): almost certainly a static museum exhibit with narration, not an engine run (snippet only).
- DVIDS audio 'ISR Tour Bf 109G-10' (https://www.dvidshub.net/audio/41601/isr-tour-bf-109g-10): seemingly a museum audio-tour item, not an engine recording (snippet only).
- AWM field recordings are CC BY-NC 3.0 AU and genuine (Richard Johnson, 2014), but they hold no German aircraft.

Next step: the owner should open the Freesound and Commons pages to confirm licence, length and whether other aircraft or crowds are audible. They could also contact FHCAM or Vintage V-12s for any Jumo 211 test-cell recording.
